record.paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
record.original_question: Can differentially private GAN mechanisms for time-series generation be improved enough to provide meaningful privacy guarantees without destroying the fidelity of the generated time-series data?

evidence.quote: Our results suggest that DP-GAN mechanisms require significant improvements for privacy-preserving time series generation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a distribution over multivariate time series $x = (x_1,\dots,x_T) \in \mathbb{R}^{T\times d}$ optionally accompanied by metadata $m \in \mathcal{M}$. A generator is a (possibly randomized) map $G_\theta$ taking a noise seed $z$ (and optionally metadata) to a synthetic sample. A training mechanism $\mathcal{A}$ takes a dataset $S = \{(x^{(i)}, m^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^n \sim \mathcal{D}^n$ and outputs trained parameters $\theta = \mathcal{A}(S)$.

Differential privacy. The mechanism $\mathcal{A}$ is $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private if, for any two datasets $S, S'$ differing in a single record and every measurable set $E$ of parameter outputs,
$$\Pr[\mathcal{A}(S) \in E] \le e^{\varepsilon}\, \Pr[\mathcal{A}(S') \in E] + \delta.$$

Fidelity. Fix a finite collection of statistics $\mathcal{T} = \{T_1,\dots,T_K\}$ where each $T_k$ maps a dataset of time series to a value in a metric space $(\mathcal{Y}_k, \rho_k)$ (e.g.\ marginal distributions, autocorrelation functions, cross-feature joint distributions, downstream classifier accuracy). For a real dataset $S$ and synthetic dataset $\tilde S$ generated by $G_\theta$, define the fidelity gap
$$\mathrm{Fid}(\theta; S) = \max_{1\le k\le K} \rho_k\!\big(T_k(S),\, T_k(\tilde S)\big).$$

Question. Does there exist a training mechanism $\mathcal{A}$ for time-series generative adversarial networks that is $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private with meaningful parameters (say $\varepsilon = O(1)$ and $\delta = o(1/n)$), and such that for natural classes of networked time-series distributions $\mathcal{D}$ the expected fidelity gap $\mathbb{E}_{S\sim \mathcal{D}^n}[\mathrm{Fid}(\mathcal{A}(S); S)]$ converges to that of a comparable non-private GAN as $n \to \infty$?

Equivalently: can differentially private GAN mechanisms for time-series generation be improved enough to provide meaningful privacy guarantees without collapsing the fidelity of the generated data on standard fidelity metrics?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has proposed concrete improvements to DP-GAN training (e.g., taking more discriminator steps per generator step, clipping decay schedules, and DP fine-tuning from public pretraining), reporting substantial fidelity gains on tabular and image data and partial gains on time-series benchmarks. However, no work conclusively establishes that DP-GAN mechanisms can simultaneously achieve standard meaningful DP parameters and non-degraded fidelity on networked time-series tasks; recent surveys and empirical studies still report a substantial privacy–fidelity trade-off, so the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Private GANs, Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Existing instantiations neglect to consider how adding noise only to discriminator updates inhibits discriminator training; taking more discriminator steps between generator steps restores parity and improves results.
status_evidence.claim: Improvements to canonical DP-GAN training procedures partially close the fidelity gap but do not resolve the question for time-series.

status_evidence.title: Differentially Private Generative Adversarial Networks for Time Series, Continuous, and Discrete Open Data
status_evidence.snippet: A differential privacy framework for privacy preserving data publishing using GANs adapted to time-series, continuous, and discrete data.
status_evidence.claim: Time-series DP-GAN frameworks exist but report nontrivial utility loss under meaningful DP budgets.

status_evidence.title: DoppelGANger (IMC 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: DP-GAN mechanisms require significant improvements for privacy-preserving time series generation.
status_evidence.claim: The original problem is posed as open.
